meeting_header: Date: 2027-03-30; Time: 16:00 PT; Duration: 45m; Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Carlos (CTO, Windward), Aisha (ML Lead), Tom (Product)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Windward AI's multilingual customer support agent. Key constraints: ~32k token context for long threads, high multilingual accuracy (EN/ES/FR/JA), tool-calling for backend lookups, and strict data residency/SOC2 requirements. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and open-model candidates (Llama 3 variants, Mistral, Mixtral/GGML variants). Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark run with sample prompts.
topics: security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Ethan from our SE team will cover the technicals. Carlos: Hey Maya, thanks. Carlos here. Aisha and Tom with me. Good to be here.
[00:18] Ethan: Great, quick agenda — understand your workload, context lengths, multilingual needs, tool calling, and then map to hosted/dedicated/private options and model candidates.
[00:30] Carlos: High level — Windward's building a customer support agent for enterprise customers, needs to ingest long chat threads, reference docs, run backend lookups (orders, entitlements), and reply in multiple languages. Latency target is sub-800ms 95th for short replies but we can tolerate 1.5s for longer generation. Cost is important; we currently pay for OpenAI for some prod workloads but thinking about open models to reduce vendor lock and cost.
[01:05] Aisha: technical specifics — average conversation history we want to include is 8-10k tokens but occasionally need 25-30k (rare peaks). We'd like 32k contexts ideally. Also Spanish and French performance are critical; Japanese for top-tier accounts. We're doing RAG so tool-calling / function calls to our order service are part of the flows.
[01:38] Ethan: ok that helps. For 32k context, we're looking at model variants that support long context out of the box or with segment-level retrieval; Llama 3 32k variants, Mistral Mixtral 32k (weird name), and a couple of optimized open models are viable. Note: some quantized GGML builds can hit lower cost but may lose some accuracy on multilingual edge cases.
[02:05] Tom: question: tool-calling — do you support structured function calls like OpenAI style? We need deterministic JSON responses back to call our APIs.
[02:15] Ethan: yes — our hosted API supports function/tool calling; we can enforce structured output with schema, and the runtime can route tool calls to your services. On dedicated/private customers we can deploy the same tooling in VPC and still provide function-call orchestration. There may be differences in latency depending on network and on-prem infra.
[02:42] Carlos: security is a big deal. we need SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, full audit logs, and for some customers, on-prem or VPC deployments with KMS/HSM integration.
[02:55] Maya: totally understood. we have SOC2 report, SSO/SAML support, fine-grained RBAC, and our Private offering supports customer-managed VPC, on-prem bundle, and KMS integrations. Ethan will send the security docs.
[03:12] Aisha: for model accuracy — we've benchmarked OpenAI's models and Anthropic on NLU tasks in Spanish and found gaps. Is there guidance on which open models perform well multilingual out-of-the-box?
[03:28] Ethan: short answer: Llama 3 family has strong multilingual coverage compared to older Llama 2, especially the later weights. Mistral 7B/Chat-like families are good for English but can drop in some low-resource languages. Mixtral (Mistral-derived larger context variants) and some community-tuned LLMs like Mosaic/Eleuther-based fine-tunes sometimes help. But the best path is to benchmark with your prompt set. We can run a controlled benchmark on Redwood Dedicated or Hosted using your prompts and sample data.
[03:58] Carlos: cost vs latency tradeoff — we'd like cheaper tokens but latency < 800ms for the short route. How do you handle batching with strict latency SLOs?
[04:12] Ethan: our runtime supports workload-aware batching and dynamic routing — we can split traffic to a low-latency pool (e.g., lower batching, prioritized) and a cost-optimized pool (higher batching). On Dedicated we can reserve a GPU pool for your low-latency SLA. We also do KV/prefix caching so repeated multi-turn chats avoid recomputing the full context on every turn.
[04:38] Tom: we have some legal/regulatory customers in EU — can you help with data residency?
[04:45] Maya: yes, region pinning and private deployment options exist. For regulated accounts we recommend Private with customer-managed network, or Dedicated zones stationed in the EU region with reserved capacity.
[04:57] Aisha: function-calling reliability — if the model makes an incorrect tool call, do you offer automatic fallbacks or human-in-the-loop routing?
[05:05] Ethan: we have canary policies and fallback models. You can define rule-based fallbacks: if confidence low or schema mismatch, route to shorter deterministic models or to a validation layer that re-checks results. We also surface token-level logs and scoring so you can detect regressions.
[05:30] Carlos: for private deployment, what's the onboarding timeline? We have a Q3 rollout target.
[05:38] Maya: Private deployments typically take 6-10 weeks depending on network approvals and infra. Dedicated is faster — often 2-4 weeks once contracts and capacity are agreed. Hosted is immediate for POC.
[05:50] Tom: any customers doing a hybrid approach — e.g., Hosted for experimentation then Dedicated for prod?
[05:56] Ethan: yes, many customers start on Hosted, run benchmarks, then move to Dedicated for predictable economics and Private for regulated clients. We support consistent model versions across environments so rollouts are simpler.
[06:10] Aisha: about quantization — we'd like to save cost with 4-bit quantization but not at the expense of hallucinations. what do you recommend?
[06:20] Ethan: 4-bit or q4f4 can reduce cost a lot. For generative tasks with structured output we recommend testing q4f4 and comparing hallucination rates on your evals. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload and flag quality regressions.
[06:40] Carlos: do you have bench data for Llama 3-32k vs Mixtral vs Mistral 7B on Spanish NLU?
[06:50] Ethan: we have internal benchmarks but they vary by prompt. we'll run a custom benchmark on your prompt set — that's the single best signal. We can run it on Hosted (fast) or Dedicated (mirrors prod).
[07:06] Tom: logistics — what info do you need from us to run the benchmark?
[07:10] Ethan: ideally: 1) 50-200 representative prompts per language, 2) expected ground truth or scoring rubric, 3) sample payloads (anonymized), 4) latency SLOs and cost targets. Aisha said she can provide that.
[07:25] Aisha: yes I'll put together 120 prompts across EN/ES/FR and a small Japanese set; will anonymize logs.
[07:33] Maya: perfect. I'll send the pricing deck and reserved capacity examples after this call. Ethan will attach the security docs and Private deployment guide.
[07:42] Carlos: about pricing — any ballpark for Dedicated reserved capacity for 4x A100 equivalent throughput?
[07:50] Maya: rough ballpark depends on model and region; I'll include examples in the deck. For planning, think of a 20-40% uplift vs pure spot/infer self-managed costs because we include orchestration, autoscaling, and SLO guarantees.
[08:05] Tom: one last question on tool-calling latency — do you support async tool calls or streaming function responses?
[08:13] Ethan: yes we support streaming and async patterns. If you need long-running lookups, we can return a provisional response and emit a follow-up event when the tool result is ready.
[08:28] Carlos: good. timeline — we're aiming for a POC in mid-May, production by September.
[08:35] Maya: sounds feasible. Next steps recap: Maya sends pricing, Ethan sends security & deployment docs, Aisha uploads prompts and sample logs, schedule technical deep-dive and benchmark.
[08:50] Tom: ok thanks everyone, this was useful.
[09:00] Maya: thanks Carlos/Aisha/Tom — we'll follow up with links. shared deck link: https://redwood.example.com/deck/windward-model-selection (note: placeholder). benchmark spreadsheet placeholder: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/windward-sample.xlsx
[09:20] Carlos: thanks, bye.
[09:25] End of recording.
